successors.name: Wei (Warring States)
successors.text: the new state 'at present-day Tang County called Zhongshan'

successors.name: Jin (Chinese state)
successors.text: Xianyu, 'centered in today's Zhending County' (Zhengding), Hebei

ledger.x: 660 BC: the Di set up Xianyu.
506 BC: the Xianyu found Zhongshan at Tang County.
506 BC: the state is Zhongshan in the record.
489 BC: Jin takes the Zhending core.

wars.name: Jin campaigns against the Xianyu and the Di towns
wars.outcome: In winter 530 Jin destroyed Fei and attacked the Xianyu capital (Xianyu page); Gu was conquered by Jin in 520; the Northern Di page has Jin attacking the White Di in the Taihang 530-520.

wars.name: Battle of Pingzhong
wars.outcome: 'In 507 BC, the Xianyu people defeated the Jin army at the Battle of Pingzhong and captured the Jin general Guan Hu.'

wars.name: Jin conquest of Xianyu
wars.outcome: Xianyu, with Wei, Qi and Lu, intervened in the 494-491 Jin civil war among the Six Ministers; 'because of this, Xianyu was attacked and conquered by the Jin commander Zhao Yang in 489 BC.'

wars.name: Wei conquest of Zhongshan
wars.outcome: Wei troops under Yue Yang conquered Zhongshan in 407 (Zhongshan page), 406 on the Northern Di page.

certainty.note: No Xianyu or Zhongshan boundary is documented on the pages; the Zhending and Tang County discs are stand-ins.
